chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us; Abu al-Qasim Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abdul Aziz al-Baghowi narrated to him; Ali ibn al-Ja'd narrated to him; Zuhair narrated to him, from Simak ibn Harb, and Ziyad ibn 'Ilqah, and Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman, all of them, from Jabir ibn Samurah, that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
There will be twelve leaders after me.

Then he said in his narration: 'Then he spoke something which I did not understand.' And some of them said in their narration: 'So I asked my father.' And some of them said: 'So I asked the people,' and they said: 'He said: They are all from Quraysh.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the twelve leaders after the Prophet according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith from Jabir ibn Samurah, recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, establishes the number and tribal origin of the twelve divinely appointed successors, affirming their Qurayshi lineage as a condition of leadership. The variant readings regarding the Prophet's final clarification highlight the transmission chain's role in preserving the specific detail that all twelve are from Quraysh, a key criterion in Shia Imamology. This narration serves as a primary textual proof for the succession of the Twelve Imams, linking the prophetic promise directly to the Ahl al-Bayt.
